observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: The receiver arrives in ECX and is copied to EBX at 0x006a3356 (MOV EBX,ECX); categories.abi.receiver names register ECX, shape R-ALIAS, offsets [0], bounds_only true. Both terminators pop sixteen bytes (RET 0x10 at 0x006a33da and 0x006a33f9), so the callee owns the cleanup of its own arguments, which excludes cdecl and fastcall; ECX carrying the receiver makes __thiscall the only consistent convention. categories.abi.conventions.confidence is INFERRED, not OBSERVED, and cross_validation records ghidra=no_information.
observed_original_abi.ordinary_stack_argument_note: The machine record lists only entry_ESP+0x8 and entry_ESP+0xc and records abstained_because [flow_not_modelled: the linear ESP walk ends at -4, so the listing is not one path; slot_gaps_present]. The listing itself shows four reads at [ESP + 0x20], [ESP + 0x24], [ESP + 0x28] and [ESP + 0x2c] after a 40-byte prologue, which are entry_ESP+0x8 through entry_ESP+0x14. All four are read once and none is written; the +0x8 and +0xc slots are the two the record does enumerate.

mechanics.body_shape: SEH prologue, four saved registers, one direct factory call, one conditional, four register-indirect transfers, two exits
mechanics.prologue: 0x006a3330 PUSH -0x1; 0x006a3332 PUSH 0x120d70a; 0x006a3337 MOV EAX,FS:[0x0]; 0x006a333d PUSH EAX; 0x006a333e MOV dword ptr FS:[0x0],ESP. A two-word record is chained onto FS:[0x0] before anything else, which categories.abi.seh_or_cookie_frame and inference V2 read as an SEH or cookie frame. No scope table is read, no landing pad exists and the listing contains no catch clause, so no language-level exception handling is claimed; the frame is modelled as two opaque words plus the displaced chain word.
mechanics.saved_registers: 0x006a3345..0x006a3348 PUSH ECX/EBX/ESI/EDI, restored at 0x006a33c7..0x006a33cb and 0x006a33ea..0x006a33ee. The saved ECX is the only one read back (0x006a33cc, 0x006a33e6), to restore the FS chain; EBX is reused as the receiver alias at 0x006a3356, so its saved copy is dead.
mechanics.frame_words: The word at [ESP + 0x18] is the scope state word: 0xffffffff from the prologue, overwritten with 0 at 0x006a3364 and back to 0xffffffff at 0x006a3385. Nothing in the listing reads it back. The word at [ESP + 0xc] is the saved ECX slot, reused from 0x006a3360 to hold the factory result.
mechanics.receiver_alias: 0x006a3356 MOV EBX,ECX -- the receiver is carried in EBX for the rest of the body. Because the alias is a different register from ECX, the literal-operand scan the validator runs over the listing finds no ECX operand at all, which is why the machine record enumerates the single receiver displacement 0 (observed through the alias) and why the reconstruction claims no receiver field offset.
mechanics.factory_call: 0x006a3358 CALL 0x00f473a0 with six words (0x38, 0x1408b44, and four nulls pushed at 0x006a334b..0x006a334e), cleaned by the caller at 0x006a335d (ADD ESP,0x18). ECX is not rewritten, so the factory's receiver is this function's own receiver. Nothing in this repository identifies 0x00f473a0, the 0x38 or the four null words; Ghidra's rendering of the same call supplies string literals that no record here corroborates and that are therefore not adopted.
mechanics.null_factory_result: 0x006a3368 CMP EAX,ESI with 0x006a336a JZ 0x006a337a. A null result skips only the 0x006a1b90 call; the body then continues with the object word still null and writes through it at 0x006a3391, 0x006a339b and 0x006a33a1, and dispatches on it at 0x006a33c1. The listing contains no second null test and the reconstruction adds none.
mechanics.create_call: 0x006a336c PUSH 0x1408b34; 0x006a3371 MOV ECX,EAX; 0x006a3373 CALL 0x006a1b90; 0x006a3378 MOV ESI,EAX. The object this body works on is the return value; it is null when the factory failed.
mechanics.word_copies: 0x006a338f..0x006a33a1 copy three words out of the descriptor returned by dispatch site one into the object at byte displacements 0x8, 0xc and 0x10, read from the descriptor at 0x0, 0x4 and 0x8. The listing interleaves the 0x006a3397 stack load between the second and third copy; that load hoists the entry_ESP+0x10 word for the transfer after the block. No record names any of the six words.
mechanics.dead_register_write: 0x006a33b5 MOV ECX,ESI writes the receiver register and no later instruction reads it: both exits take their words from the stack (0x006a33cc, 0x006a33e6). It is recorded here rather than reproduced in the source, which has nowhere to put a write whose value is never observed.
indirect_call_sites: 0x006a338d: CALL EDX -- slot word at byte displacement 0x10 of the table word at displacement 0 of the entry_ESP+0x8 object; receiver is that object (ECX=EDI at 0x006a3383); no stack word; result is the descriptor the three copies read

0x006a33b3: CALL EDX -- slot word at byte displacement 0x24 of the receiver's own table word; receiver is this function's receiver (ECX=EBX at 0x006a33b1); four stack words: entry_ESP+0x10, entry_ESP+0x14, the created object, the entry_ESP+0x8 object; AL of the result is tested
0x006a33c5: CALL EAX -- slot word at byte displacement 0 of the created object's table word; no stack word; nothing the transfer returns is read; success path only
0x006a33e4: CALL EAX -- slot word at byte displacement 0x8 of the same table, one entry further in; single immediate word 1; failure path only; nothing the transfer returns is read
mechanics.indirect_call_corroboration: categories.abi.dispatch.indirect_calls is 4, which agrees with the four register-indirect sites the listing shows. This is the only dispatch count in the record that is corroborated: categories.function_identity.vtables names vtable:0x014091a0 while dependencies.vtable_reference_count is 0, so that association is a classifier claim and is not used here.
mechanics.slot_naming: No slot member is named anywhere in the reconstruction. No record in this repository names what any of the four slots holds; each is addressed by the byte displacement the listing shows and read into a function-pointer local before the call.
mechanics.slot_cleanup_inference: INFERENCE, not observation: the frame is balanced across all four transfers (no ADD ESP follows any of them and the epilogues account for exactly the pushes), so each callee must have popped what it was handed. The three slot types are therefore declared __thiscall with the receiver as their first parameter. If a slot target turns out to clean up in the caller, those three types are what changes.
mechanics.direct_call_corroboration: dependencies.edges records exactly these two as direct-call out-edges of this record, and the listing holds exactly these two CALL immediates. There is no JMP anywhere in the 77 instructions, so there is no tail call and no intra-procedural jump to exclude.

mechanics.data_address_caveat: Neither address is corroborated. dependencies.data_reference_count for this record is 0 and the xref export carries no data-reference edge type, so there is no second machine side to check either address against, and no record says what either one points at. They are reproduced as the opaque addresses the listing pushes; Ghidra's decompilation renders them as two string literals, and that rendering is not adopted because nothing here grounds it. The validator's GLOBALS check therefore WARNs on this target by design, and that WARN is the correct verdict, not a defect in the reconstruction.
mechanics.out_parameter: entry_ESP+0xc is written through exactly once, at 0x006a33bb/0x006a33bf, on the success path only. On the failure path the object built at 0x006a3378 is dropped without ever being published through it.
mechanics.success_exit: 0x006a33bb..0x006a33da: store the object through entry_ESP+0xc, dispatch slot at displacement 0 on it, restore the chain word, ADD ESP,0x10, RET 0x10 with AL set to 1.
mechanics.failure_exit: 0x006a33dd..0x006a33f9: dispatch the slot at displacement 0x8 on the object with the immediate 1, restore the chain word, ADD ESP,0x10, RET 0x10 with AL zeroed.
mechanics.control_flow: Two conditional branches, JZ 0x006a337a at 0x006a336a and JZ 0x006a33dd at 0x006a33b9. Both targets lie inside the body span 0x006a3330..0x006a33f9, so the branch graph is closed inside the listing.
mechanics.displacement_convention: Every displacement in the reconstruction is passed as a value to load_word/load_slot/store_word rather than written inline as `object + n`, and no member name appears anywhere. The slot byte displacements (0x10, 0x24, 0x00, 0x08), the destination word displacements (0x8, 0xc, 0x10) and the source word displacements (0x0, 0x4, 0x8) are table and payload offsets on objects that are not the receiver; the only receiver word the body reads is its own table word, at displacement 0, which is exactly the single displacement categories.abi.receiver.offsets enumerates. FIELDS/OFFSETS passing therefore says that no receiver field offset is claimed beyond the machine-derived bound -- not that any field layout is confirmed, which bounds_only leaves open.

return_semantics.observation: MOV AL,0x1 at 0x006a33c9 on the success path and XOR AL,AL at 0x006a33ec on the failure path; the two exits differ only in that byte, the chain restore and the preceding transfers.
return_semantics.ownership: The body creates no reference count of its own. The object built at 0x006a3378 is handed to four dispatched slots, published through entry_ESP+0xc on the success path, and dropped without publication on the failure path. Whether dispatch site three releases it and dispatch site four reports it is not established by any record here, so no ownership claim is made.
return_semantics.residual_word_state: Only AL is written on either exit, so the upper three bytes of the returned word are whatever the last register-indirect transfer left in EAX. A reconstruction returning a wider integral would be asserting those bytes; this one does not.
return_semantics.lifetime: Nothing in this body establishes how long the object stays valid, and no record in this repository names the two direct callees, so the object they produce is identified only by the fact that it is returned.

unresolved_questions: What do the two data-segment addresses hold, and are the byte reads enough to call them grounded? 0x1408b44 is pushed as the second word of the 0x00f473a0 call and 0x1408b34 as the single word of the 0x006a1b90 call. The xref export records data_reference_count 0 for this record and carries no data-reference edge type, so the export corroborates neither address and GLOBALS stays WARN. A direct byte read of the same binary (GhidraMCP /read_memory, recorded in mechanics.data_segment_addresses) shows NUL-terminated ASCII at both: App/PropertyList/Create at 0x1408b44 and CreateResource at 0x1408b34. That agrees with Ghidra's decompilation, which renders the same two arguments as string literals, and the agreement is now two machine-side reads of the same bytes rather than one decompiler inference. What is still unestablished: the C++ type of either object, whether either is a const char* or a char array or a tagged structure whose first bytes spell that text, and the read/write mode the validator asks for. No type is declared in the candidate source.

What are the four dispatch slots? Byte displacement 0x10 of the entry_ESP+0x8 object's table (0x006a338d), 0x24 of the receiver's own table (0x006a33b3), 0 (0x006a33c5) and 0x8 (0x006a33e4) of the created object's table. No record in this repository names any of them, and the record's own vtable association (0x014091a0) comes with vtable_reference_count 0, so it is a classifier claim and not a slot identity.

What are the two direct callees? 0x00f473a0 is a six-word caller-cleaned call whose second word is a data address and whose first is 0x38, and 0x006a1b90 takes one word and a receiver in ECX and returns the object the body works on. Neither is identified by any record in this repository, and the object they produce is known only by the fact that the body returns it.

Why does the body not test the created object for null after a null factory result? A null result takes the JZ at 0x006a336a, leaves the object word null, and the body then writes through it at 0x006a3391, 0x006a339b and 0x006a33a1 and dispatches on it at 0x006a33c1. Either the factory never returns null in practice, or a caller guarantees otherwise, or the path is simply not defended; the listing gives no way to tell.

Do the four slot callees clean up their own stack words? The frame is balanced across all four transfers with no ADD ESP after any of them, so callee cleanup is an inference, and the three slot function-pointer types are declared __thiscall on that basis. A resolved slot target would confirm or refute it.

Is the entry_ESP+0x8 object the same thing the receiver's slot at 0x24 expects as its first stack word? The listing passes the same EDI/ESI/EDI word to both dispatches, and Ghidra names it both an IRecord and a source of the three copied words. No record establishes the relationship.

What does the scope record at 0x006a3330 chain onto FS:[0x0] do? 0x120d70a is pushed as its scope table and never read by the listing, and no record names it. The reconstruction models the chain as two opaque words and claims no handler, no catch clause and no landing pad.

conditions: The original process is run under Wine with a live App::cPropManager receiver, a live entry_ESP+0x8 object and a writable entry_ESP+0xc word.
A trace records the four dispatch targets actually taken at 0x006a338d, 0x006a33b3, 0x006a33c5 and 0x006a33e4 for at least one receiver subtype, which is what would resolve the slot questions.
A trace records whether 0x00f473a0 can return null, which is what would settle the undefended null path at 0x006a3391.
A trace records whether the object stored through entry_ESP+0xc on success is released by dispatch site three or reported by dispatch site four, which is what would settle the ownership question.
